files.purpose: Use titlebar space for navigation and drag profiles across long lists
files.previous_behavior: Profiles had arrow controls and navigation sat below an otherwise empty native titlebar.
files.new_behavior: Profile grip supports multi-position drag, insertion marker and automatic edge scrolling; rendering pauses during drag. Existing navigation and URL controls share a compact header with window buttons.
files.data_impact: Sends profile IDs and placement intent only; no credential data changes.
files.access_control_impact: none: trusted chrome messages retain existing profile isolation and permissions.
risks: Native drag feedback and accessibility of direct manipulation vary by device; arrow buttons remain available.
files.rollback: Revert this commit and rebuild Oinzi; redirect the desktop shortcut to the previous executable. Saved profile order remains compatible.

production_safety.operational_data: No operational profiles or credentials were inspected or changed during development; tests used synthetic profile data.
production_safety.schema_migration: none: existing profile list format retained.
external_side_effects: Local build under native/publish-compact; desktop shortcut points to this build. Active application is left running unchanged.

verification.evidence: Headless Playwright: no page errors, header fits widths 780 and 1380, minimize command routes, p0 drops after p3 and drag state clears.
All 21 native assertions passed, including PLUCK workspace preservation.

verification.command: dotnet publish native/native.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -p:PublishSingleFile=true -o native/publish-compact -p:NoWarn=MSB3277 -v quiet

residual_risks: Live desktop window dragging, resizing, multiple monitor DPI and auto-scroll interaction were not manually exercised. Custom maximize button does not reproduce Windows snap-layout hover UI.
Existing silent profile-save failure behavior remains.
